entries.odia: ଲଙ୍କା— ଗଡୁଁ ଯେତେକ ଜାତ, ସମସ୍ତେ ଅସୁରଙ୍କ ସୁତ
entries.title: One verdict for everyone
entries.literal_meaning: All who are born from Lanka’s fortress are sons of asuras.
entries.explanation: The force falls on “all”: a shared place becomes a single verdict about everyone born there. The dictionary supplies the totalizing word and quotation; its Lanka entry separately identifies the mythological capital. Our critical reading notices how quickly this image shuts out individual differences. It can help us examine a sweeping accusation, but birthplace or descent does not establish anyone’s character.
entries.meaning_odia: କଥାର ଜୋର “ସମସ୍ତେ” ଉପରେ—ଗୋଟିଏ ଜାଗାରେ ଜନ୍ମ ହେଲେ ସମସ୍ତଙ୍କୁ ଏକ ରାୟରେ ବାନ୍ଧିଦିଆଯାଉଛି। ଅଭିଧାନର ଲଙ୍କା ଶବ୍ଦରେ ପୌରାଣିକ ରାଜଧାନୀର ଅର୍ଥ ମଧ୍ୟ ଅଛି। ଆମର ସମାଲୋଚନାତ୍ମକ ପଢ଼ାରେ, ଏହି ଚିତ୍ର ଦେଖାଏ କିପରି ଗୋଷ୍ଠୀର ନାମରେ ବ୍ୟକ୍ତିର ଭିନ୍ନତା ଲୁଚିଯାଏ। ଜନ୍ମସ୍ଥାନ ବା ବଂଶରୁ ମଣିଷର ଚରିତ୍ର ସ୍ଥିର ହୁଏ ବୋଲି ଆମେ ଏହି ରାୟକୁ ଗ୍ରହଣ କରୁନାହୁଁ।
entries.english_summary: Our critical reading questions a single verdict imposed on a whole group.
entries.odia_summary: ଗୋଟିଏ ନାମରେ ସମସ୍ତଙ୍କୁ ଦୋଷୀ ଭାବିବାର ରାୟକୁ ଆମ ପଢ଼ା ପଚାରେ।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: After one team member breaks a promise, a friend declares that the whole team is alike. Another quotes the Lanka line and asks whether they have just made the same sweeping judgment. The expression is being examined critically, not endorsed as a rule about the team.
entries.cultural_context: 212713 sense2 is lexical context only. Mythological imagery is not evidence about a present-day population; no event, epic authorship or origin of this saying is established.

entries.odia: ଶତିକଈ ପୁରସ୍ତମ ଗଲା, ତୁଣ୍ଡ଼ କଥା କହି କହି ମଲା
entries.title: A taunt that follows the speaker
entries.literal_meaning: Shatikai went to Purastama and died talking and talking.
entries.explanation: The repeated talking carries the taunt to an exaggerated ending. The dictionary explicitly marks Shatikai as a satirical feminine term for a lying or talkative woman; this is an insult, not a neutral portrait. Our reading follows how the verse makes speech swallow the whole journey. Its verbal energy can be appreciated while questioning its gendered target and refusing to treat women’s speech as an inherent fault.
entries.meaning_odia: “କହି କହି”ର ପୁନରାବୃତ୍ତିରେ କଥା ଚାଲିଥାଏ, ଶେଷରେ ମରିବାର ଅତିରଞ୍ଜନ ଆସେ। ଅଭିଧାନ ଶତିକଈକୁ ମିଛ କହୁଥିବା ବା ବାଚାଳା ସ୍ତ୍ରୀ ପ୍ରତି ବ୍ୟଙ୍ଗଶବ୍ଦ ବୋଲି ଦେଇଛି; ଏହା ନିରପେକ୍ଷ ବର୍ଣ୍ଣନା ନୁହେଁ। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ, ଯାତ୍ରାକୁ ପଛରେ ପକାଇ କଥା କହିବାଟି ସବୁକିଛି ହୋଇଯାଏ। ଧ୍ୱନିର ରସ ବୁଝିବା ସହିତ ନାରୀଙ୍କ କଥାକୁ ସ୍ୱଭାବଗତ ଦୋଷ କରୁଥିବା ଟାହିକୁ ମଧ୍ୟ ପଚାରିହୁଏ।
entries.english_summary: A gendered taunt exaggerates relentless talking; our reading questions its target.
entries.odia_summary: କଥାର ପୁନରାବୃତ୍ତି ରସ ତିଆରି କରେ, କିନ୍ତୁ ନାରୀଙ୍କୁ ଟାହିର ଲକ୍ଷ୍ୟ କରିବା ପ୍ରଶ୍ନଯୋଗ୍ୟ।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: During a discussion of old sayings, someone quotes this line about a woman who speaks at length. Another listener enjoys the repeated sound but asks why the criticism singles out women. They discuss whether interruption, rather than gender, is the actual problem. No historic conversation is claimed.
entries.cultural_context: 227729 defines Purastama as Puri and as a personal name. Literal translation retains the word; no pilgrimage, identified woman, actual death or named poet is inferred.
